events.title: Spanish Inquisition holds its first auto-da-fé in Seville
events.description: Six people convicted of secretly practising Judaism were burned at the stake after a public ceremony in Seville. Autos-da-fé became the Inquisition's most notorious public ritual.
events.html: Six people convicted of secretly practising Judaism were burned at the stake after a public ceremony in Seville. Autos-da-fé became the Inquisition's most notorious public ritual.

events.title: Domingo de Salazar becomes the first bishop of Manila
events.description: The Spanish Dominican friar Domingo de Salazar was appointed the first Bishop of Manila, then newly annexed to the Spanish Empire; he served until 1594.
events.html: The Spanish Dominican friar Domingo de Salazar was appointed the first Bishop of Manila, then newly annexed to the Spanish Empire; he served until 1594.

events.title: James II becomes king on the death of Charles II
events.description: Charles II died at Whitehall and his Catholic brother succeeded as James II of England and VII of Scotland. Fears of a Catholic dynasty led to his overthrow in the Glorious Revolution of 1688.
events.html: Charles II died at Whitehall and his Catholic brother succeeded as James II of England and VII of Scotland. Fears of a Catholic dynasty led to his overthrow in the Glorious Revolution of 1688.

events.title: France signs an alliance with the United States
events.description: In Paris, Benjamin Franklin and his fellow commissioners signed treaties of alliance and commerce with France. French troops, money and naval power proved decisive in the war for independence.
events.html: In Paris, Benjamin Franklin and his fellow commissioners signed treaties of alliance and commerce with France. French troops, money and naval power proved decisive in the war for independence.

events.title: First American Colonization Society settlers sail for Africa
events.description: The ship Elizabeth left New York carrying 86 free Black Americans bound for West Africa. Their settlement efforts led to the founding of Liberia.
events.html: The ship Elizabeth left New York carrying 86 free Black Americans bound for West Africa. Their settlement efforts led to the founding of Liberia.

events.title: Treaty of Waitangi signed in New Zealand
events.description: British officials and more than 40 Māori chiefs signed the treaty at Waitangi. Differences between its English and Māori texts over sovereignty remain central to New Zealand law and politics.
events.html: British officials and more than 40 Māori chiefs signed the treaty at Waitangi. Differences between its English and Māori texts over sovereignty remain central to New Zealand law and politics.

events.title: British women over thirty win the vote
events.description: The Representation of the People Act gave the vote to women over 30 who met property qualifications, about 8.4 million women. Equal voting rights with men followed in 1928.
events.html: The Representation of the People Act gave the vote to women over 30 who met property qualifications, about 8.4 million women. Equal voting rights with men followed in 1928.

events.title: Elizabeth II becomes Queen on the death of George VI
events.description: The 25-year-old princess learned of her father's death while in Kenya. She reigned for 70 years, the longest of any British monarch, until her death in 2022.
events.html: The 25-year-old princess learned of her father's death while in Kenya. She reigned for 70 years, the longest of any British monarch, until her death in 2022.
